[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][vc_column_text css_animation="bounceIn" css=""]

I’ve marked who each event is actually for, so you spend the travel budget on the right room.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width="1/3"][vc_column_text css_animation="bounceIn"]

The Datalabs Agency is a Melbourne-based data visualization consultancy founded in 2012 that delivers corporate training workshops (Power BI, Tableau, data storytelling), dashboard design, and BI style guides for clients including Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, and UPS. Conferences are where data teams sharpen the craft — and when the budget doesn’t stretch to Las Vegas, an in-house workshop brings the sharpening to your office instead.

DDAC packs 2,500+ analytics people into Disney World, 14–16 September.

Do not let the Mickey ears fool you: DDAC draws 2,500+ executives, managers and analysts from 250+ organisations for genuinely serious content on revenue management, pricing, forecasting and decision science. This year’s confirmed keynotes include mathematician Matt Parker and machine-learning author Eric Siegel, alongside Disney and Coca-Cola practitioners. Registration is open, and it sells out — the venue is Disney’s Coronado Springs Resort, which does no harm to the case for bringing the family. New name, same tribe: Coalesce has rebranded as dbt Summit for 2026 as dbt broadens from analytics engineering into the AI-data mainstream. This is the home conference of the analytics engineering movement — the people who decide how your metrics get defined and shipped — live at The Cosmopolitan with a virtual option. The final 2026 stop on Gartner’s Data & Analytics circuit, at the Grand Hyatt Mumbai. Gartner summits are strategy events for data leaders — analyst one-on-ones, governance and AI-roadmap content rather than hands-on technique. Big Data LDN fills Olympia London on 23–24 September — the UK’s flagship data show.

My best-in-Europe pick. Big Data LDN takes over both the Grand and National halls at Olympia London — the UK’s largest data, analytics and AI gathering, mixing a huge expo floor with a dense free conference programme. It is the rare big show where registration has historically cost nothing, which makes it the best value-per-airfare on the European calendar. If you can only do one European event in 2026, this is the one I’d book. DATA ANALYTICS 2026 runs in Barcelona from 27 September to 1 October, onsite or virtual.

The academic option: the fifteenth IARIA conference on data analytics methodology, co-located with seven sibling conferences as the NexTech 2026 congress. Expect peer-reviewed papers and technical rigour rather than keynote theatre — you go to read the research and meet the researchers. The virtual participation option makes it the cheapest way on this list to sample the field’s academic frontier from your desk. Ai Everything Global lands at ADNEC Abu Dhabi on 6–7 October.

The Gulf’s government-backed AI mega-show has moved from Dubai to Abu Dhabi, rebranded as Ai Everything Global under organiser KAOUN. [/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row bg_check=”row-background-dark” css=”.vc_custom_1696657787022{background-color: #2f2e3a !important;}”][vc_column]

This is my verified calendar of the best data analytics and data science conferences for 2026 and 2027 — every date on this page was checked against the conference’s own site this month, and the graveyard of events that quietly died since last year has been cleared out (details at the bottom).

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″][vc_column_text css_animation=”bounceIn” css=””]

The spread is wider than ever: mega technical summits (Databricks, Snowflake), hands-on training conferences (ODSC), executive strategy events (Gartner, ANA), a free community unconference in 27 cities (MeasureCamp) — and the AI wave running through all of them. I’ve marked who each event is actually for, so you spend the travel budget on the right room.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner width=”1/3″][vc_column_text css_animation=”bounceIn”]

The Datalabs Agency is a Melbourne-based data visualization consultancy founded in 2012 that delivers corporate training workshops (Power BI, Tableau, data storytelling), dashboard design, and BI style guides for clients including Mercedes-Benz, Adidas, and UPS. Conferences are where data teams sharpen the craft — and when the budget doesn’t stretch to Las Vegas, an in-house workshop brings the sharpening to your office instead.

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner]

Disney Data & Analytics Conference

[vc_column_text css=””]

14–16 September 2026

Orlando, U.S.A.

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/4″]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

DDAC packs 2,500+ analytics people into Disney World, 14–16 September.

Do not let the Mickey ears fool you: DDAC draws 2,500+ executives, managers and analysts from 250+ organisations for genuinely serious content on revenue management, pricing, forecasting and decision science. This year’s confirmed keynotes include mathematician Matt Parker and machine-learning author Eric Siegel, alongside Disney and Coca-Cola practitioners. Registration is open, and it sells out — the venue is Disney’s Coronado Springs Resort, which does no harm to the case for bringing the family.
[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column]

dbt Summit 2026

[vc_column_text css=””]

15–18 September 2026

Las Vegas, U.S.A. (hybrid)

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

dbt Summit — the conference formerly known as Coalesce — hits Las Vegas 15–18 September.

New name, same tribe: Coalesce has rebranded as dbt Summit for 2026 as dbt broadens from analytics engineering into the AI-data mainstream. This is the home conference of the analytics engineering movement — the people who decide how your metrics get defined and shipped — live at The Cosmopolitan with a virtual option. If your team touches a modern data stack, someone from it should be in this room (or on this stream).
[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/4″]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column]

Gartner Data & Analytics Summit Mumbai

[vc_column_text css=””]

21–22 September 2026

Mumbai, India

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/4″]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

Gartner’s Mumbai summit runs 21–22 September — the last Gartner D&A stop of 2026.

The final 2026 stop on Gartner’s Data & Analytics circuit, at the Grand Hyatt Mumbai. Gartner summits are strategy events for data leaders — analyst one-on-ones, governance and AI-roadmap content rather than hands-on technique. The 2027 series is already announced: Orlando (8–10 March), London (10–12 May) and Sydney (7–8 June) — the Orlando edition gets its own entry below, and Australian readers will find Sydney covered in my data visualization conferences guide.
[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column]

Big Data LDN

[vc_column_text css=””]

23–24 September 2026

London, England

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

Big Data LDN fills Olympia London on 23–24 September — the UK’s flagship data show.

My best-in-Europe pick. Big Data LDN takes over both the Grand and National halls at Olympia London — the UK’s largest data, analytics and AI gathering, mixing a huge expo floor with a dense free conference programme. It is the rare big show where registration has historically cost nothing, which makes it the best value-per-airfare on the European calendar. If you can only do one European event in 2026, this is the one I’d book.
[/vc_column_text]

[vc_column_text css=””]

27 September – 1 October 2026

Barcelona, Spain (hybrid)

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/4″]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

DATA ANALYTICS 2026 runs in Barcelona from 27 September to 1 October, onsite or virtual.

The academic option: the fifteenth IARIA conference on data analytics methodology, co-located with seven sibling conferences as the NexTech 2026 congress. Expect peer-reviewed papers and technical rigour rather than keynote theatre — you go to read the research and meet the researchers. The virtual participation option makes it the cheapest way on this list to sample the field’s academic frontier from your desk.
[/vc_column_text]

Ai Everything Global

[vc_column_text css=””]

6–7 October 2026

Abu Dhabi, U.A.E.

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

Ai Everything Global lands at ADNEC Abu Dhabi on 6–7 October.

The Gulf’s government-backed AI mega-show has moved from Dubai to Abu Dhabi, rebranded as Ai Everything Global under organiser KAOUN. This is a deal-making event — investors, ministries, startups and enterprise buyers at national-strategy scale — rather than a practitioner conference. Go to understand where sovereign AI money is flowing (and there is a lot of it flowing through the UAE); bring business cards, not notebooks.
[/vc_column_text]

AI & Big Data Expo Europe

[vc_column_text css=””]

19–20 October 2026

Amsterdam, Netherlands

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/4″]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

AI & Big Data Expo Europe returns to RAI Amsterdam on 19–20 October.

AI & Big Data Expo Europe is the European stop of the TechEx circuit at RAI Amsterdam, co-located with IoT, cyber-security and digital-transformation expos — one badge, five shows. It is vendor-heavy by design, which is exactly its use: comparing platforms and integrators side by side in an afternoon. The circuit’s Global edition moves to Olympia London on 3–4 February 2027, and North America follows in San Jose on 16–17 June 2027.
[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column]

ODSC AI West 2026

[vc_column_text css=””]

27–29 October 2026

Burlingame / San Francisco, U.S.A.

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

ODSC AI West runs 27–29 October in the San Francisco Bay Area — the hands-on one.

My best-for-training pick. ODSC (now rebranded ODSC AI) is built around workshops rather than keynotes — hands-on sessions on RAG pipelines, LLM orchestration and agentic AI that working data scientists can take back to their desks on Monday. West 2026 runs at the Hyatt Regency SF Airport in Burlingame; its sibling ODSC AI East returns to Boston in May 2027. If your goal is skills rather than networking, spend your money here.
[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/4″]

[/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row gap=”20″ bg_check=”row-background-dark” css=”.vc_custom_1696657851210{background-color: #2f2e3a !important;}”][vc_column]

Machine Learning Week Europe

[vc_column_text css=””]

16–18 November 2026

Munich, Germany

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/4″]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

Machine Learning Week Europe runs in Munich, 16–18 November.

“Technical depth, practical lessons, no sales pitches” is the promise Machine Learning Week Europe makes, and the format backs it up: a dedicated masterclass day (16 November) followed by two days of case studies with extended Q&A. This is the European event for ML practitioners who ship models rather than talk about them — smaller and more focused than the expo circuit, and priced accordingly.
[/vc_column_text]

[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column]

Big Data Conference Europe

[vc_column_text css=””]

24–27 November 2026

Vilnius, Lithuania (hybrid)

[/vc_column_text]
[/vc_column][vc_column width=”1/6″][/vc_column][vc_column width=”5/12″][vc_column_text]

Big Data Conference Europe runs in Vilnius, 24–27 November — onsite or online.

Big Data Conference Europe is four days in Vilnius at human scale: an onsite workshop day (24 November) then three hybrid conference days on big data, ML and AI at Forum Cinemas Vingis. No vendor-summit gloss, sensible Baltic pricing, and the online option covers the talks if the flight doesn’t make sense from your part of the world. A good European bookend to the year for engineers and analysts.
[/vc_column_text]
